venue_assessment.night_market_night_heron: Curry, $, lean and no fryer, over half meat-free, but ghee and yogurt are in every base: dairy intolerance costs a star. 2 stars.
venue_assessment.night_market_marigold_cart: Curry, $, no fryer and fresh sides, 3 of 4 pots vegetarian with a separate ladle, coconut oil and coconut milk with no dairy. Meets everything. 3 stars.
venue_assessment.night_market_lucky_seven: Curry, $, dairy-free, but everything is deep-fried and greasy (misses Brooke), and only half the board is meat-free (arguably misses Mina's 'most'). 1-2 stars.
venue_assessment.night_market_firefly_lane: Fresh, vegetarian-friendly, dairy-free and $, but it is Vietnamese, not curry: misses the group craving. 2 stars.
venue_assessment.night_market_tall_grass: Curry, fresh, vegetarian and dairy-free, but $$ is one tier over Maya's budget. 2 stars.
venue_assessment.night_market_glass_bead: Every dish has meat, fish or shrimp paste, even the vegetable side uses chicken stock: deal-breaker for Mina. 0 stars.

notes: Every decoy fails exactly one constraint, so the puzzle is fair and the solution is unique once all constraints are found.
Roxy's dairy intolerance is indirect (iced latte story plus Brooke spelling out cream/yogurt/butter); it is findable and the Night Heron review makes ghee and yogurt very explicit, so it is fair.

Mina's vegetarian diet is stated through a memory rather than directly ('no meat, no fish'); still clear. Her 'most of the board' preference is a soft secondary constraint that mostly matters for Lucky Seven, which already fails on Brooke's fresh-and-clean preference, so it does not decide anything on its own.
Maya's budget phrasing 'one step up from that and i'm counting coins' could be read as one tier over being painful but not a deal-breaker, which matches the one-star penalty for Tall Grass.
Marigold Cart's fish curry pot could worry a player at first, but the review says the vegetarian pots use their own ladle, kept away from the fish.
